claim: Fails when the builder and the owner launch on or after 16 January 2027: PP 33/2026, the implementing regulation of UU 27/2022 (in force that day, 225 articles on impact assessments, data protection officers, cross-border transfer and breach notice), is in no Section Record, so the consent text, privacy policy and breach steps follow the law alone and may miss duties the regulation adds. The 2026-11-27 amendment check covered only the law itself.

evidence.quote: processing a child's personal data needs a parent's or guardian's consent (UU 27/2022 Art. 25)

chain: then the privacy policy and consent text (D-017, D-050, D-051) are written against the law alone
and then a duty added by PP 33/2026 (for example the breach-notice route or transfer conditions) is missing at launch, and the copy and milestones must be reworked after the build
fix: Read the official PP 33/2026 text (jdih.setneg.go.id) for a small controller with low-risk data; record the duties that apply (privacy-policy content, transfer, breach notice, DPIA threshold) in S3 as a cited decision, and add the in-force date 16 January 2027 to the regulation notes.

claim: Fails when a feature turns out unused after launch (for example few players self-cancel through F-03 and keep messaging the admin): no in-MVP feature names a kill criterion, so nothing says which result would drop or rethink it, and the owner keeps maintaining it.
chain: then each feature stays in later versions whatever its use
and then the owner cannot tell which feature to cut when the free limits or the builder's time run short
fix: Add one line per in-MVP feature to the S7 record: the user job (who, what for) and a kill criterion, e.g. F-03 'fewer than 1 in 5 cancellations go through the page after 2 months → rethink the cancel flow'.
class_reason: no earlier scored run of this scope

claim: Fails when a bot or a looping script loads the schedule more than 100,000 times in a day: every page, booking included, returns Error 1027 until 07.00 WIB, the plan prices no bad month and names no request-rate rule or alert, so the evening's bookings go back to WhatsApp.

evidence.quote: Requests over the daily limit get Error 1027 until the reset at midnight UTC

chain: then the site is down for the rest of the day
and then players lose trust in the link and return to WhatsApp chats
fix: Add one realistic bad month to the cost table (bot traffic or a retry loop at the daily limit: Rp 0 but an outage until 07.00 WIB) and the mitigation: a Cloudflare rate-limiting rule on the schedule route plus the 'site down → book by WhatsApp' fallback text.

claim: Fails when Turnstile's siteverify is unreachable: the server refuses every online booking and the plan names no fallback (what the player sees, and that the admin takes the booking by WhatsApp through F-02).

evidence.quote: Cloudflare Turnstile Free | USD 0; unlimited challenges

chain: then online booking stops while Turnstile is down
and then players message the admin, which F-02 can absorb only if the fallback is written
fix: Write the fallback: on a Turnstile error show 'Pemesanan online sedang gangguan. Hubungi admin lewat WhatsApp' with the venue's WhatsApp link; the admin books through F-02.

claim: Fails when the venue later changes the .biz.id address or the booking-link format after players have saved and shared links in WhatsApp groups: no one-way-door list says which steps are costly to undo (domain, link format, data already stored in Singapore, PSE record) or who holds each handle.

evidence.quote: Own domain: .biz.id bought now, Rp 9.900 first year and Rp 60.000 per year renewal

impact_reason: Each listed step can be undone at small cost (update three profile links, keep an old route); the gap is that it is not traced, not that harm is permanent.
fix: Add a short one-way-door list to S5: domain (registrar login on the venue email, auto-renew), confirmation and cancel link format (kept stable for the life of the app), data stored in Singapore (consent D-051), PSE record; each with its undo cost and handle holder.

claim: Fails when the owner reaches the launch task and learns that PSE Lingkup Privat registration goes through OSS and needs an NIB (business ID) first: D-026 says the procedure was re-verified in S5, but S5 holds no PSE check, and no account, key or approval the build needs (NIB, OSS login, PSE registration, Cloudflare, Supabase, registrar, Turnstile keys) is listed with its owner and lead time.

evidence.quote: PSE Lingkup Privat registration with Komdigi before public opening; launch task; procedure re-verified in S5

chain: then the public opening waits on an NIB and an OSS application whose lead time nobody planned
and then the venue either opens unregistered (warning letters and access blocking, U-03) or delays launch
fix: Research the current PSE route (Komdigi guide s.komdigi.go.id/pendaftaranpseprivat, OSS, NIB prerequisite) and write an accounts-and-approvals list with owner (the venue email per D-022) and lead time; correct the D-026 'procedure re-verified in S5' wording.

claim: Fails when Cloudflare or Supabase changes its free plan: the plan names paid fallbacks on the same vendors but not the cost of moving to another host or database.
fix: Add one line per core vendor: SvelteKit has adapters for other hosts (about one agent session to move), and Supabase is plain Postgres (pg_dump plus re-pointing the keys; Supabase Auth users need a re-invite).

claim: Fails when the admin forgets the password: the reset email goes through Supabase's default SMTP, which sends only to project-team addresses, at most 2 messages per hour, best-effort and meant for non-production use, and the plan cites none of this or names a second recovery route.

evidence.quote: Admin "forgot password" sends a reset email to the admin email

chain: then a reset email is delayed or lost
and then the admin cannot see the day's schedule until it arrives
fix: Cite the Supabase default-SMTP limits and record a recovery route: the venue email owns the Supabase account (D-022), so the owner can set a new password from the Supabase dashboard; a custom SMTP sender is a later option.

claim: Fails when the owner checks at month 6 whether the app was worth it: 'no one-by-one booking chats' has no baseline and no measure, so nobody can tell whether booking chats fell from today's level.

evidence.quote: Success: zero double bookings and no one-by-one booking chats for the admin

chain: then success is judged by feeling
and then the owner cannot decide whether to keep the app, pay for a plan, or return to WhatsApp
fix: Record the measure: count booking chats in one week before launch; after launch read the share of online versus admin-entered bookings from the weekly CSV (F-05) each month; target, e.g., at least 70% online by month 6, and zero clashes.

claim: Fails when a blocked number stays in blocked_numbers forever: the plan erases names and numbers 90 days after play (D-025) but keeps the block list until the admin unblocks, so a WhatsApp number is held with no retention limit, against the retention promise in the privacy policy.

evidence.quote: masked on the booking page (08••••••7890); erased after 90 days; block list kept until unblocked

chain: Two no-shows add a number to blocked_numbers
The daily job erases bookings after 90 days but never touches the block list
The privacy policy's 90-day promise is untrue for blocked players under PP 33/2026
fix: Blocked numbers expire 180 days after the block unless the admin renews it; the daily job deletes expired rows; state the period in the privacy policy, SECURITY.md and SPEC/data-model.md.
